title: Writing a finite tape block
statement: Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$, let $j$ be one of the $k$ work tapes, and let $x$ be a binary input. Suppose a configuration $c$ has live writer state, tape $j$ contains a nonblank symbol at each cell from its head position through the next $m-1$ cells, and the cell $m$ positions ahead is blank. For every binary word $w$ of length $m+1$, running the specified writer machine from $c$ under $w$ ends in its done state; the tape contents are those of $c$ with the cells from the initial head position up to, but not including, the cell $m$ positions ahead replaced by the first $m$ bits of $w$, and the head is advanced by $m$. Moreover, no run from $c$ under a word of length less than $m+1$ is in the done state.
hypotheses_covered: $j$ is a work-tape index among the $k$ tapes
$c$ has state equal to the live writer state
The next $m$ cells from the head position are all nonblank
The cell $m$ positions ahead is blank
